## Glyphling 1.0.0

Download `Glyphling-Setup-1.0.0.exe` below and run it. It updates an existing installation in place, keeping settings, themes and position. If you already have Glyphling, it will also offer this update by itself.

A tiny animated dot-matrix companion for your Windows desktop: music visualizer, timer, weather, clock, calendar and system stats, all in one glowing circle.

### Highlights
- **One circle, six modes**: clock, calendar, music, Focus timer, weather and system stats. Turn the dial (or the mouse wheel) to switch; right-click the circle to go back to the mascot.
- **Music**: follows the apps you choose (running apps or any .exe) and controls only those. The circle's volume moves exactly the app's own slider in the Windows volume mixer, never the system volume. Cover art is drawn on the LEDs, in your theme colors or in its own colors.
- **Calendar**: your Google Calendar through a secret iCal link, plus your own events, reminders and tasks added with a right-click on a day.
- **Focus timer** with configurable focus and break lengths, stopwatch and countdown.
- **System**: CPU, RAM, disks (real drive letters and names), NVIDIA GPU and CPU temperature. If no temperature source exists, Settings can install LibreHardwareMonitor for you, with your consent.
- **Position**: the circle is the anchor and always stays on screen; quick positions for corners, edges and center; the panel and the mode label flip toward the free side.
- **Looks**: themes and a theme editor, 12/24 hour and °C/°F, circle resolution 512, 1024 or 2048 points, first-run tutorial.
- **Updates**: Glyphling checks the GitHub releases by itself and installs new versions over the current one, only when you agree.
- **Installer**: custom setup that installs for your user (no administrator rights), lets you choose the folder, updates in place and uninstalls cleanly.

### Notes
- Fixed the music panel redrawing every second when nothing is playing, and the panel no longer rewrites unchanged text every frame.

The setup is not signed yet: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway"). Glyphling is not affiliated with Nothing.
